fire: Quail avoid dense brush during the breeding season (Jones 1964, Crawford and Bolen 1976, Taylor 1980).
Deer use slopes less than flat ground (Schaller 1967, Khan 1994, Green and Wells 2001).
Fecundity rises with body size in many insects (Murphy, 1983; Moore and Singer, 1987).
Nest success depends on cover height (Davison 1940, Copelin 1963, Riley 1978).
Grazing changes plant cover quickly (Brown 1985, Hart and Lowe 1992, Ortiz 2004).
Rodent numbers follow seed crops (Ellis 1971; Garelick and Hunt 1988; Ross 1999).
Frogs breed earlier in warm years (Beebee 1995, Reading 1998, Gibbs and Breisch 2001).
Owls hunt more on moonlit nights (Clarke 1983, Kotler and Brown 1991, Penteriani 2011).
quiet: Quail avoid dense brush during the breeding season, as many hunters know.
Deer use slopes less than flat ground, especially in deep snow.
Fecundity rises with body size in many insects, though not in all.
Nest success depends on cover height and the number of nearby predators.
Grazing changes plant cover quickly when herds stay too long in one field.
Rodent numbers follow seed crops closely from one year to the next.
Frogs breed earlier in warm years and later after cold winters.
Owls hunt more on moonlit nights when prey is easier to see.
